a05.reason: Emits zero edits and its only content is a factually false finding that would destroy valid Layer-A data if actioned. The author affirms the auditor's premise ("The finding is correct on the facts") that tokens[0] 出/for and tokens[1] かけ are "stray"/"corruption", and prescribes "dropping tokens[0] and tokens[1]" at the tokenizer level. Verified against corpus/sentences/bank.json: those two entries are split_mode="A" short-unit alternates of the split_mode="C" token at position 8 (出かけ/でかけ), an intentional second segmentation layer the a05.json projection discards when it flattens the array to a single i index. The concat invariant holds over split_mode C for all 5565 sentences in the bank (0 mismatches); a naive all-token concat "fails" on 638 records precisely because they carry A-split alternates (1389 A tokens bank-wide), so the objection is a projection artifact, not a defect. The correct disposition was to refute it as unfounded; instead the submission records a deletion recommendation that, if applied, strips legitimate A-split segmentation. Same false claim is appended as a "separate note for the pipeline" in sent:gen-580e51dbf624's refutation (about its A 5 水曜 + A 5 日, the A-split of C 5 水曜日) and must be discarded there too, though that item's actual edits are sound and ship fine.

a16.reason: tokens[5].gloss.pt-BR ships a corrupted Japanese form: "...dentro do composto やってくら" ends in ら (U+3089) instead of る (U+308B). やってくら is not a word, so the very edit meant to fix the false lexical claim about やる now teaches a nonexistent compound, and it contradicts its own sibling paths in the same patch — gloss.en and both conjugation_note values all correctly write やってくる. A learner comparing the en and pt-BR gloss sees two different verbs. Rule 6 (Japanese readings correct in context) and rule 4 (locale consistency) both fail. Corroborating signal that the edit was never authored: its "why" is literally the string "placeholder", so this value went out unjustified and unchecked. The remaining three edits for this sentence are sound and would have resolved the objection; only the pt-BR gloss needs re-authoring as "fazer (やる); aqui só como forma -て dentro do composto やってくる" with a real rationale.

a23.reason: The only edit sets translation.en to the empty string, which is not a shippable value and does not resolve the objection. The objection is that a patch ADDED an AI-authored English into the Layer-A locale-object texts.translation on a gen=false record, shadowing the Tatoeba source en and introducing a translation.en key 23 of 25 records in the batch do not carry. Emptying the string does not remove the key, so the schema drift the objection names survives, and it now ships a blank learner-facing Layer-A translation field - a renderer/exporter treats presence-with-empty as content, so the record would show an empty English translation, which is worse than the defect. The author's stated rationale is also factually wrong: "" does not restore "the pt-BR-only shape the record had before the patch" (before had no en key at all; after has en=""). The auditor hint is deliberately empty and the objection states the remedy is quarantining the record; the author's own why concedes the Layer-A English cannot be supplied without fabrication and that quarantine is out of scope - i.e. no safe field-level value exists, so the correct action was to emit NO edit for this record rather than an empty value.

edits.new: A expressão temporal 〜の後で (depois de) marca quando a ação ocorreu: 夕飯の後で = depois do jantar, com で indicando o momento. Em seguida vem o objeto 食器を (a louça) e o verbo 片付けた (arrumei/guardei), no passado. A ordem é tempo + objeto + verbo, típica do japonês.

edits.new: Once more the target pattern 〜方（かた）: つかう (to use) → つかい + 方 = つかい方 (way of using / how to use). このきかいのつかい方 = "the way of using of this machine", with この ("this") and の linking きかい to つかい方. を marks this way as the object, and しりたいです expresses desire: しる (to know) in the stem + たい (desiderative) + です, "I want to know".

edits.new: Outra vez o padrão-alvo 〜方（かた）: つかう (usar) → つかい + 方 = つかい方 (modo de usar / como usar). このきかいのつかい方 = "o modo de usar desta máquina", com この ("esta") e の ligando きかい a つかい方. を marca esse modo como objeto, e しりたいです expressa desejo: しる (saber) na raiz + たい (desiderativo) + です, "quero saber".

edits.new: Estrutura simples tópico + adjetivo: この (este) modifica お茶 (chá), marcado como tópico por は, e o predicado é o adjetivo-i 温い. O advérbio もう ('já') indica que o estado mudou para morno. edits.new: The structure is [A の B は C です]: 彼女の踊り (her dance) is the topic marked by は, and きれい (beautiful) is a 形状詞 (na-adjective) linked to the copula です. The の links 彼女 (she) to 踊り (dance) in a relation of possession. Note that きれい takes です directly and, despite ending in い, does not inflect like an i-adjective, which is typical of na-adjectives.

edits.new: A estrutura é [A の B は C です]: 彼女の踊り (a dança dela) é o tópico marcado por は, e きれい (bonito/a) é um 形状詞 (adjetivo-na) ligado à cópula です. edits.new: O tópico 先生 (professor) é marcado por は. Aqui 丁寧 aparece como adjetivo-na modificando um substantivo, por isso vem com な (丁寧な日本語 = 'um japonês cuidadoso/educado'). 日本語 é o objeto marcado por を, e o verbo principal é 話す (falar) no presente polido com ます. Contraste: antes de substantivo, 丁寧 recebe な; em posição adverbial, recebe に (丁寧に).

edits.new: In dates, 七日 (written here ７日) is read as one whole word, なのか: the なの part sits on the numeral and か on 日.
edits.why: The auditor's clean alternative (merging ７ and 日 into one token) is a retokenization, which is out of scope here, so the residual hazard is a learner seeing なの over the numeral with no explanation. This note states the whole-word reading at exactly the token where the furigana renders, so なの is presented as a fragment of なのか rather than as an independent reading of seven.

edits.new: Em datas, 七日 (aqui escrito ７日) se lê como uma palavra inteira, なのか: a parte なの fica no numeral e か em 日.
edits.why: Locale parity with the en note added at the same token; without it the pt-BR learner gets the bare なの furigana and no account of where it comes from.

refuted.why: Not authored as requested, on two grounds. (1) The proposed remedy is structural: merging tokens[4] ７ and tokens[5] 日 into a single ７日 token changes token surfaces and the token count, which the pipeline cannot express and the hard rules forbid; no field value can produce it. (2) The premise that なの is simply a second wrong reading is too strong. Date counters decompose morpheme by morpheme: 四日 よっ+か, 五日 いつ+か, 六日 むい+か, 八日 よう+か, 十日 とお+か, so 七日 なの+か assigns なの to the numeral and か to the day counter. That is the same slicing the auditor accepted for 四つ = よっ + つ in sent:gen-6425cd1dd284, so refusing it here would leave the batch internally inconsistent. The genuine wrong reading (なな) is gone, sentence kana/romaji are correct, tokens[5].role already teaches 七日 = なのか, and the new note on tokens[4] closes the furigana gap. Separate note for the pipeline: this item has the same phantom-head-token defect flagged in sent:gen-61579a61ed0a, tokens[0] 水曜/すいよう and tokens[1] 日/び, an alternative segmentation of the 水曜日 that already appears at tokens[7]; concat of surfaces is 水曜日今月の７日は水曜日だ, not the jp. It needs the same tokenizer-level fix and cannot be repaired by field authoring.

edits.new: A frase é uma pergunta curta e informal, sem verbo expresso (a cópula 'é' fica subentendida). 「この変な匂い」é o sujeito/tópico: この (este) + 変な (estranho) + 匂い (cheiro). 変 é um adjetivo do tipo な, por isso aparece com な antes do substantivo. 「は」marca o tópico e 「何」(o quê) é a pergunta.

edits.new: The sentence is a short, informal question, with no expressed verb (the copula 'is' is understood). 「この変な匂い」is the subject/topic: この (this) + 変な (strange) + 匂い (smell). 変 is a na-type adjective, which is why it appears with な before the noun. 「は」marks the topic and 「何」(what) is the question.

edits.new: The sentence follows the basic Japanese order: topic/subject first, then the object, then the verb. The subject is 小さな子ども ('little child'), marked by でも ('even'), which gives the sense of 'even a...'. The object その名前 ('that name') takes を, and the verb 知っている is in the 〜ている form (知る + て + いる), which with 知る expresses the state of 'knowing/being acquainted with', not an ongoing action.

edits.new: A frase segue a ordem japonesa básica: primeiro o tópico/sujeito, depois o objeto e, por fim, o verbo. O sujeito é 小さな子ども ('criancinha'), marcado por でも ('até mesmo'), que dá o sentido de 'mesmo uma...'. O objeto その名前 ('esse nome') leva を, e o verbo 知っている está na forma 〜ている (知る + て + いる), que com 知る expressa o estado de 'saber/conhecer', e não uma ação em andamento.

O verbo final 祈ろう está na forma volitiva de 祈る ('rezar, torcer'), que expressa 'vamos...' ou uma intenção/exortação. Aqui 祈る tem o sentido figurado de 'torcer/esperar' por algo. A estrutura é [sujeito が verbo と] + [verbo volicional].

Pattern: a request with 〜をください + a quantity expression.

O núcleo é o verbo 鳴らせ: é a forma imperativa do verbo transitivo 鳴らす ('fazer soar'), e a partícula final よ reforça a ordem. edits.new: The pattern here is not existential いる (居る). ピザ is inanimate, so this いる is the verb 要る ('to need, to be needed'), and what が marks is the thing needed, which is the grammatical subject of 要る: ピザがいる人 = 'a person who needs pizza'. Existential 居る is only for living beings and could never take ピザ as its subject. The whole relative clause modifies the noun 人 (person). It is a colloquial call, with さあ opening it and the lengthening ー at the end sounding like a shout to the group.
edits.why: 要る is intransitive, so が marks its grammatical subject; the field said 'the inanimate subject ピザ' and 'whose object is marked by が' in the same breath, contradicting itself as well as the token label. Aligned on the accurate analysis, which also keeps the real teaching point (an inanimate cannot be the subject of existential 居る). The build-facing 'target pattern' framing is gone from the learner text too.
